notes: **General features:** eukaryotic, heterotrophic (absorptive nutrition), cell wall of chitin, filamentous hyphae forming mycelium, reproduce by spores, store food as glycogen or oil.
**Phycomycetes:** asexual spores (zoospores) in sporangia. Coenocytic (multinucleate) hyphae. Examples: Rhizopus (bread mould), Phytophthora (late blight).
**Ascomycetes:** sac fungi. Sexual spores (ascospores) formed in asci inside ascocarps. Examples: yeast, Penicillium, Aspergillus, morels.
**Basidiomycetes:** club fungi. Sexual spores (basidiospores) produced externally on basidia in basidiocarps. Examples: mushrooms, bracket fungi, rusts, smuts.
**Deuteromycetes:** imperfect fungi. No known sexual stage. Reproduction by conidia. Examples: Alternaria, Trichoderma, Epidermophyton.
